title: AI Alignment via Incentives and Correction
abstract: arXiv:2605.01643v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We study AI alignment through the lens of law-and-economics models of deterrence and enforcement. In these models, misconduct is not treated as an external failure, but as a strategic response to incentives: an actor weighs the gain from violation against the probability of detection and the severity of punishment. We argue that the same logic arises naturally in agentic AI pipelines. A solver may benefit from producing a persuasive but incorrect answer, hiding uncertainty, or exploiting spurious shortcuts, while an auditor or verifier must decide whether costly monitoring is worthwhile. Alignment is therefore a fixed-point problem: stronger penalties may deter solver misbehavior, but they can also reduce the auditor's incentive to inspect, since auditing then mainly incurs cost on a population that appears increasingly aligned.   This perspective also changes what should count as a post-training signal. Standard feedback often

translated_title: 通过激励与纠正实现AI对齐
translated_abstract: 我们通过法律与经济学中的威慑与执行模型来研究AI对齐问题。在这些模型中，不当行为不被视为外部故障，而是对激励的战略性回应：行为者会权衡违规所得收益与被发现的概率及惩罚的严厉程度。我们认为同样的逻辑在智能体（agentic）AI流水线中会自然出现。求解器可能通过生成有说服力但不正确的答案、隐藏不确定性或利用虚假捷径而获益，而审计者或验证者则必须决定昂贵的监控是否值得。因此，对齐是一个不动点问题：更强的惩罚可能会阻止求解器的不当行为，但也可能降低审计者进行检查的动机，因为此时审计主要只是在一个看起来越来越对齐的群体上产生成本。这一视角还改变了什么应被视为训练后信号。标准反馈通常……
tldr: 该论文将法律经济学的威慑与执行理论引入AI对齐研究，提出对齐本质上是一个求解器与审计者之间的激励博弈不动点问题——过度惩罚求解器反而可能削弱审计者监督的动力。
en_tdlr: This paper applies law-and-economics deterrence models to AI alignment, framing alignment as a fixed-point problem in the incentive game between solvers and auditors, where overly strong penalties on solvers can paradoxically erode auditors' motivation to inspect.
